text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) arrested doctor at Prijedor hospital Milan Kovacevic and killed former Prijedor police chief Simo Drljaca in "Operation "Tango" launched against indicted war criminals.

- Biljana Plavsic, president of the Bosnian Serb republic, said she cannot be responsible for the nation's reaction to NATO action in letter of protest addressed to General William Crouch, commander SFOR.

- High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, agrees that single Bosnian currency cannot carry the symbols which represent the culture of another country, says co-chairman in the Council of Ministers Haris Silajdzic.

- The long-awaited agreement on the establishment of a joint police force in the Neretva-Herzegovina canton was signed yesterday in Mostar. The basis for the national balance of the police will be the 1991 census.

- U.S. diplomat Robert Beecroft says those who do not respect the joint police agreement cannot expect assistance from the United States, which will do everything to convince the international community not to assist those who are not cooperative.

- Reaching agreement on the establishment of a joint police force in the Neretva canton clears the way for a summit between Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and the chairman of the Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, which could happen within a week, officials said.
- Survivors of Srebrenica plan to commemorate two year anniversary of fall of enclave, when thousands of unarmed Moslems were massacred.

- With the arrest of indicted war criminals the international community clearly proved that it stands behind the concept of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a single state, says Silajdzic, co-chairman in the Council of Ministers. --Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
